title: Muthoot Finance Q1 Profit Jumps 43% as Gold Loan Book Approaches ₹2 Lakh Crore
excerpt: India's largest gold loan financier extends its growth streak into FY27, driven by record gold prices and RBI's new gold loan framework that favours organised lenders.
body:
• Muthoot Finance reported a 43% jump in Q1 FY27 standalone profit, with gold loan assets under management approaching the ₹2 lakh crore milestone, according to CNBCTV18.
  • The result extends a remarkable FY26, when the company posted its highest-ever annual profit of ₹10,134 crore — a 95% year-on-year increase.
  • Gold loan AUM grew 50% in FY26 to ₹1.63 trillion, fueled by record gold prices and tighter unsecured lending norms from the RBI.
  • New RBI gold loan guidelines are expected to benefit organised players like Muthoot by strengthening transparency and customer confidence.

Q1 FY27 Keeps the Momentum

Muthoot Finance, India's largest gold loan financier, reported a 43% jump in standalone profit for the April–June quarter of FY27, with gold loan assets under management closing in on the ₹2 lakh crore mark, according to CNBCTV18. The result signals that the company's multi-quarter growth streak shows no signs of slowing, even as gold prices have consolidated after a steep rally.

The Q1 performance builds on FY26, which was a record-breaking year across virtually every metric. For the full year ending March 2026, Muthoot posted standalone profit after tax of ₹10,134 crore, up 95% from ₹5,201 crore in FY25, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. Total loan AUM reached ₹1,62,826 crore, a 50% increase.

Gold Prices and Regulatory Tailwinds

The company's growth has been turbocharged by two forces. Gold prices, which have surged past ₹1 lakh per 10 grammes, directly boost the collateral value underlying gold loans, enabling larger disbursements against the same quantity of pledged gold. Simultaneously, the RBI's tighter norms on unsecured personal lending have pushed borrowers toward gold-backed credit as a more accessible alternative, according to Reuters.

"The new gold loan guidelines are a positive step for the industry and are expected to accelerate the formalisation of the gold loan sector by strengthening transparency, governance, and customer confidence in organised players."

— George Jacob Muthoot, Chairman, Muthoot Finance

In Q4 FY26, standalone PAT surged 105% year-on-year to ₹3,086 crore, while net interest margins expanded to 13.38% from 11.27% a year earlier, per Reuters. The company added 177 new branches during that quarter alone.

Portfolio Implications

Muthoot Finance shares have climbed 55% over the past year and 232.5% over three years, closing at ₹3,531 ahead of the FY26 results, according to Livemint. The stock has consistently outperformed rival Manappuram Finance, which has diversified more aggressively into non-gold segments like microfinance and MSME lending.

Analysts remain divided on valuation. Jefferies expects standalone gold AUM to grow 21% in FY26 and raised earnings estimates, while Motilal Oswal flagged that Muthoot's valuation looks "rich for the deep cyclicality in its gold loan growth," warning that any volatility in gold prices could reverse the trend, per Livemint.

Beyond Gold

Muthoot is gradually building non-gold lending capacity. Subsidiary Muthoot Money saw AUM grow over 200% in Q1 FY26, with substantial contributions from gold loans as it wound down vehicle finance. Belstar Microfinance, another subsidiary, is scaling its gold loan branches from 15 to 50. The non-gold share of the consolidated portfolio is expected to reach 15–20%, up from 13–14%, according to company guidance.

What to Watch

Gold price trajectory remains the key variable. While elevated prices support AUM growth, a correction could trigger higher defaults and compress margins. The RBI's evolving gold loan framework will also shape competitive dynamics, particularly between NBFCs and banks entering the gold-backed lending space.
nri_angle: Muthoot Finance is widely held by NRI investors and its gold loan growth reflects broader trends in Indian household credit and gold-backed lending that affect diaspora portfolios.
